title: Expander Hierarchies for Normalized Cuts on Graphs

problem.claim: The work addresses computing expander decompositions and hierarchies for graph problems, including normalized cut graph clustering.

gap.claim: Practical adoption of expander decompositions has been hindered by their inherent intricacies and large hidden factors in asymptotic running times.

contributions.claim: An algorithm for computing expander decompositions and their hierarchies.
A normalized cut graph clustering solver that uses the expander decomposition and hierarchy algorithm as its core component.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe their algorithm as the first practically efficient algorithm for computing expander decompositions and their hierarchies.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report demonstrating the effectiveness and utility of their approach through a normalized cut graph clustering solver.

narrative_sequence.summary: Expander decompositions have advanced understanding of classical graph problems and produced fundamental theoretical results.
Practical adoption has been limited by conceptual intricacy and large hidden asymptotic running-time factors.
The authors introduce a practically efficient algorithm for expander decompositions and hierarchies and use it in a normalized cut graph clustering solver.

source_observation.claim: The authors connect an algorithmic improvement in expander decomposition with a downstream normalized cut clustering solver.

interpretation.claim: Reducing practical overhead in a foundational graph primitive can enable its use as a component in an applied optimization system.

application.claim: When adapting theoretically valuable graph techniques, evaluate whether implementation efficiency is sufficient for integration into an end-to-end solver.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this integration is effective beyond the authors' reported demonstration.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the algorithm's running time, hidden factors, or approximation guarantees.
The abstract does not provide datasets, baselines, quantitative results, or experimental conditions.
The abstract does not describe the expander hierarchy construction or normalized cut solver in technical detail.
